text:
A VPN is a private tunnel between your device and the internet. Everything you send goes through it in scrambled form, so people on the same Wi-Fi or your internet provider can't read it.

Here is the path:

Your device scrambles (encrypts) your data and sends it to the VPN company's computer.
That computer unscrambles it and passes it on to the website you wanted.
The website sees the VPN's address instead of yours, so it can't tell where you really are.

It helps on public Wi-Fi and hides your browsing from your internet provider. It doesn't make you fully anonymous, though. The VPN company can still see your activity, so pick one you trust.
